segments.line: Mo grabs your arm. 'Come with us to the station. Your mom will find you there. '
But
what if she doesn't? What if she's waiting for you at home, and the buses leave without her?
Ellie looks at you. She's waiting for you to decide. You
decide. You
put Ellie on the back of your bike, and you ride the other way.
Hour twenty- six. Light is slower
than your bike. Your bike light can't keep up with you. You are riding faster than your own beam, into the dark.
Halfway there, a car comes around the corner, way too fast. The
driver can't see you in time, because the light from your bike reaches him too late. He
swerves at the very last second. Ellie
squeezes you so hard you can barely breathe. You keep riding. At
the hospital, everything you see is old. You
spot your mom at the end of a long hallway and run toward her.
But when you get there, she's gone. You
were looking at where she was a minute ago. So you do the only thing that still works fast.
You shout. 'Mom! ' And from right
behind you, she shouts back. She
hugs you both so hard it hurts. Then she looks at her watch.
Eleven forty. She grabs a bike from the rack outside. You
ride like you've never ridden. At
the station, you see the last bus still waiting at the stop.
But that's old light. It already left. Ellie
screams. The
sound reaches the bus before any light could. Its
brakes squeal. The door opens. Mo is inside, waving like crazy.
Mo's dad pulls you up the steps, and the cat goes in last. The bus
rolls down a ramp, into a tunnel, under the ground.
Behind you, the city goes dark.
